name: Joshua

objectives.text: Identify Joshua as the leader God chose after Moses to bring Israel into the promised land
Retell how the walls of Jericho fell when Israel followed God's instructions to march and shout
Recall that Rahab hid the spies and that she and her family were saved when Jericho fell
Retell how Israel crossed the Jordan on dry ground and set up twelve stones to remember what God had done
Explain from Joshua how God kept His promise to give Israel the land He had sworn to Abraham
Explain how God's command to Joshua to be strong and courageous rests on God's presence and on meditating on His Law
Explain Achan's sin and how it brought defeat at Ai and judgment on his household
Outline the four main sections of Joshua as entering the land, conquering the land, dividing the land, and renewing the covenant
Compare the report of the spies in Joshua 2 with the report of the spies in Numbers 13 and 14
Explain why Israel was circumcised and kept the Passover at Gilgal before the conquest began
Describe Joshua's encounter with the commander of the LORD's army and what it shows about who leads Israel's battles
Explain how the Gibeonites deceived Israel and why the text faults Israel for not asking counsel of the LORD
Analyze the central, southern, and northern campaigns of the conquest using a map of Canaan
Analyze Rahab's confession of the LORD and how the New Testament presents her as an example of faith and an ancestor of Christ
Interpret the account of the sun standing still in its literary context and compare ways Reformed interpreters have explained it
Connect the allotment of tribal territories to God's promises to the patriarchs and to Caleb's inheritance
Explain the purpose of the cities of refuge and the Levitical cities in Israel's life in the land
Explain the meaning of herem, things devoted to destruction, from its commands in Deuteronomy and its use in Joshua
Analyze the dispute over the altar of witness and how the tribes resolved it to preserve the unity of worship
Analyze how Joshua's statements of total conquest relate to its notices of land that remained unconquered
Evaluate arguments about the justice of the Canaanite conquest using the biblical reasons given for judgment and the sparing of Rahab and Gibeon
Analyze the covenant renewals at Mount Ebal and Shechem and Joshua's charge to choose whom Israel will serve
Evaluate how archaeological evidence from sites such as Jericho, Ai, and Hazor bears on the dating and history of the conquest
Evaluate how ancient Near Eastern sources such as the Amarna Letters and their references to the Habiru inform the setting of Joshua
Analyze ways the Reformed tradition reads Joshua as a type of Christ who leads His people into their inheritance
Synthesize the theme of rest from Joshua with its development in the Psalms and Hebrews in a written argument

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (Joshua as leader, Jericho, Rahab, Jordan crossing, God's promise, Achan, spies comparison, campaigns, sun standing still, allotment, herem, morality of conquest, Hazor archaeology, Amarna Letters, rest). Replaced 'Apply the verse' with an explanation of the command's basis in God's presence and the Law, and turned the conquest defense into an evaluation of arguments from the text. Added missing competencies: book structure, Gilgal circumcision and Passover, commander of the LORD's army, Gibeonite deception, Rahab in the NT, cities of refuge and Levitical cities, altar of witness, total conquest versus remaining land, covenant renewals at Ebal and Shechem, and Joshua as a type of Christ. Split the Jordan crossing from Jericho, added verse-level anchors throughout, and cited confessions only where they state the doctrine (WCF 5.1, 5.3, 7.5, HC Q103).
